before: Autoboxing converts an int value to an Integer reference; unboxing retrieves the primitive int. Collections use reference types, so ArrayList<Integer> relies on these conversions when storing or retrieving ints.
An Integer reference can be null; int cannot. Unboxing null throws NullPointerException. A presence check must occur before the conversion, not after it.

after: Boxing wraps a primitive number, such as int, as an object value, such as Integer. Unboxing gets the primitive value back. Java often performs these conversions automatically, including when integer values enter or leave collections.
An Integer reference can be null, but an int cannot. Trying to unbox null throws NullPointerException. Check for null before reaching the conversion.

For two Integer references, == checks whether they point to the same object. Java may reuse wrapper objects, so do not use this to compare their numbers. For a non-null wrapper, equals compares its number with another wrapper of the same type.
The program prints 5. boxed is present, so Java unboxes four into value and then adds one.
The quiz makes boxed null. The check chooses the other branch before any unboxing is attempted.
